route.reason: Mechanism of action of atorvastatin (Lipitor) is described in the FDA drug label, not trial registry records.

draft.text: Lipitor (atorvastatin) is a selective, competitive inhibitor of HMG-CoA reductase, the rate-limiting enzyme that converts HMG-CoA to mevalonate, a precursor of sterols including cholesterol [label:atorvastatin:mechanism_of_action:0]. In animal models, it lowers plasma cholesterol and lipoprotein levels by inhibiting HMG-CoA reductase and cholesterol synthesis in the liver, and by increasing the number of hepatic LDL receptors on the cell surface to enhance LDL uptake and catabolism [label:atorvastatin:mechanism_of_action:0]. It also reduces LDL production and the number of LDL particles [label:atorvastatin:mechanism_of_action:0].
